question: ____________ denotes the largest timestamp of any transaction that executed write(Q) successfully.
explanation: The most common method for doing ordering transaction is to use a timestamp-ordering scheme.

question: The _____________ ensures that any conflicting read and write operations are executed in timestamp order.
explanation: The most common method for doing ordering transaction is to use a timestamp-ordering scheme.

question: The __________ requires that each transaction Ti executes in two or three different phases in its lifetime, depending on whether it is a read-only or an update transaction.
explanation: A concurrency-control scheme imposes the overhead of code execution and possible delay of transactions. It may be better to use an alternative scheme that imposes less overhead.

question: This validation scheme is called the _________ scheme since transactions execute optimistically, assuming they will be able to finish execution and validate at the end.
explanation: A concurrency-control scheme imposes the overhead of code execution and possible delay of transactions. It may be better to use an alternative scheme that imposes less overhead.

question: Snapshot isolation is a particular type of ______________ scheme.
explanation: It has gained wide acceptance in commercial and open-source systems, including Oracle, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server.

question: Snapshot isolation is used to give
options: A) Transaction a snapshot of the database
B) Database a snapshot of the transaction
C) Database a snapshot of committed values in the transaction
D) Transaction a snapshot of the database and Database a snapshot of committed values in the transaction
explanation: The data values in the snapshot consist only of values written by committed transactions.

question: Lost update problem is
options: A) Second update overwrites the first
B) First update overwrites the second
C) The updates are lost due to conflicting problem
explanation: Lost update problem has to be resolved.

question: Under first updater wins the system uses a __________ mechanism that applies only to updates.
explanation: Reads are unaffected by this, since they do not obtain locks.

question: When a transaction Ti attempts to update a data item, it requests a _________ on that data item.
explanation: Reads are unaffected by this, since they do not obtain locks.

question: Each of a pair of transactions has read data that is written by the other, but there is no data written by both transactions, is referred to as
explanation: Write skew is the issue addressed here.

question: An application developer can guard against certain snapshot anomalies by appending a ______ clause to the SQL select query.
explanation: Adding the for update clause causes the system to treat data that are read as if they had been updated for purposes of concurrency control.

question: ARIES uses a ___________ to identify log records, and stores it in database pages.
explanation: LSN is used to identify which operations have been applied to a database page.

question: ARIES supports ___________ operations, which are physical in that the affected page is physically identified, but can be logical within the page.
explanation: The deletion of a record from a page may result in many other records in the page being shifted, if a slotted page structure is used.

question: ______________ is used to minimize unnecessary redos during recovery.
explanation: Dirty pages are those that have been updated in memory, and the disk version is not up-to-date.

question: __________ scheme that records only information about dirty pages and associated information and does not even require of writing dirty pages to disk.
explanation: It flushes dirty pages in the background, continuously, instead of writing them during checkpoints.

question: Whenever an update operation occurs on a page, the operation stores the LSN of its log record in the _______ field of the page.
explanation: Each page maintains an identifier called the PageLSN.

question: There are special redo-only log records generated during transaction rollback, called _________ in ARIES.
explanation: These serve the same purpose as the redo-only log records in our earlier recovery scheme.

question: The __________________ contains a list of pages that have been updated in the database buffer.
explanation: Dirty pages are those that have been updated in memory, and the disk version is not up-to-date.

question: ___________ determines which transactions to undo, which pages were dirty at the time of the crash, and the LSN from which the redo pass should start.
explanation: The analysis pass finds the last complete checkpoint log record, and reads in the DirtyPageTable from this record.

question: __________ starts from a position determined during analysis, and performs a redo, repeating history, to bring the database to a state it was in before the crash.
explanation: The redo pass repeats history by replaying every action that is not already reflected in the page on disk.

question: ______________ rolls back all transactions that were incomplete at the time of crash.
explanation: It performs a single backward scan of the log, undoing all transactions in undo-list.

question: Which lock should be obtained to prevent a concurrent transaction from executing a conflicting read, insert or delete operation on the same key value.
explanation: Operations acquire lower-level locks while they execute, but release them when they complete; the corresponding transaction must however retain a higher-level lock in a two-phase manner to prevent concurrent transactions from executing conflicting actions.

question: Once the lower-level lock is released, the operation cannot be undone by using the old values of updated data items, and must instead be undone by executing a compensating operation; such an operation is called
explanation: It is important that the lower-level locks acquired during an operation are sufficient to perform a subsequent logical undo of the operation.

question: Which of the following is used for undo operations alone?
options: D) Physical logging and Physical log records
explanation: If the operation inserted an entry in a B+-tree, the undo information U would indicate that a deletion operation is to be performed, and would identify the B+-tree and what entry to delete from the tree. Such logging of information about operations is called logical logging.

question: Redo operations are performed exclusively using
options: D) Both Physical logging and Physical log records
explanation: Logging of old-value and new-value information is called physical logging.

question: To perform logical redo or undo, the database state on disk must be operation ___________ that is, it should not have partial effects of any operation.
explanation: Data structures such as B+-trees would not be in a consistent state, and neither logical redo nor logical undo operations can be performed on an inconsistent data structure.

question: An operation is said to be __________ if executing it several times in a row gives the same result as executing it once.
explanation: Operations such as inserting an entry into a B+-tree may not be idempotent, and the recovery algorithm must therefore make sure that an operation that has already been performed is not performed again.

explanation: Undo erases all the changes and redo makes the deleted changes.

question: The remote backup site is sometimes also called the
explanation: We can achieve high availability by performing transaction processing at one site, called the primary site, and having a remote backup site where all the data from the primary site are replicated.

question: Remote backup system must be _________ with the primary site.
explanation: We can achieve high availability by performing transaction processing at one site, called the primary site, and having a remote backup site where all the data from the primary site are replicated.

question: The backup is taken by
options: C) Sending all log records from primary site to the remote backup site
D) Sending selected records from primary site to the remote backup site
explanation: We can achieve high availability by performing transaction processing at one site, called the primary site, and having a remote backup site where all the data from the primary site are replicated.

question: When the __________ the backup site takes over processing and becomes the primary.
explanation: When the original primary site recovers, it can either play the role of remote backup, or take over the role of primary site again.

question: The simplest way of transferring control is for the old primary to receive __________ from the old backup site.
explanation: If control must be transferred back, the old backup site can pretend to have failed, resulting in the old primary taking over.

question: The time to process the remote backup can be reduced by
explanation: If the log at the remote backup grows large, recovery will take a long time. The remote backup site can periodically process the redo log records that it has received and can perform a checkpoint, so that earlier parts of the log can be deleted.

question: A _______________ configuration can make takeover by the backup site almost instantaneous.
explanation: In this configuration, the remote backup site continually processes redo log records as they arrive, applying the updates locally.

question: A transaction commits as soon as its commit log record is written to stable storage at the primary site. This is
explanation: The problem with this scheme is that the updates of a committed transaction may not have made it to the backup site, when the backup site takes over processing.

question: A transaction commits as soon as its commit log record is written to stable storage at the primary and the backup site. This is
explanation: The problem with this scheme is that transaction processing cannot proceed if either the primary or the backup site is down.

question: If only the primary is active, the transaction is allowed to commit as soon as its commit log record is written to stable storage at the primary site. This is
explanation: This scheme provides better availability than does two-very-safe, while avoiding the problem of lost transactions faced by the one-safe scheme.
